name: Roasted Oysters With Bacon and Parmesan

ingredients.name: minced flat-leaf parsley, plus more for garnish
fresh raw oysters, about 3 inches long, well scrubbed

instructions.primary_message: Gently crumple and uncrumple two 61-cm lengths of aluminum foil. Place 1 piece in a rimmed baking sheet and the second piece on a large serving platter; cover foil on platter with a clean dish towel for presentation, if desired. (Alternatively, you can line a rimmed baking sheet with a 1.5-cm layer of rock salt.)
In a medium skillet over medium heat, cook bacon until crisp and fat is rendered, 5 to 7 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer bacon to a plate; pour off all but 1 tablespoon bacon fat.

Add 1 tablespoon butter and garlic to skillet; cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add cream and mustard; bring to a simmer and reduce to a thickened consistency, 1 to 2 minutes. Off heat, whisk in Parmesan until melted and smooth; set aside.

In a food processor, pulse panko bread crumbs and parsley until finely mixed. Add cream and parmesan mixture, bacon, lemon juice,and remaining 1 tablespoon butter and pulse until just combined, emulsified, and glossy. Season with salt and pepper (go light—bacon and Parmesan are salty). The mixture should resemble thick hollandaise or warm mayo—spreadable, not runny.

Shuck 1 oyster at a time, discarding the top shell and loosening the oyster from the bottom shell. Gently flip oyster over, so plump side is now top, while keeping as much liquor as possible. Nestle into the foil nest on rimmed baking sheet.

Adjust oven rack to 15 cm below the broiler element and preheat the broiler on high. Distribute topping evenly over oysters in shell. Bake until topping begins to bubble and brown and oysters are warmed through, 4 to 10 minutes. Serve immediately, passing lemon wedges at the table.

schema_metadata.keywords: roasted oysters, oysters, Roasted Oysters With Bacon and Parmesan

description: These roasted oysters with bacon and Parmesan are rich, briny, smoky, and perfect for holidays, parties, and special occasions.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 1 teaspoon lemon juice, plus lemon wedges for serving

Optional substitutions: Dijon mustard → whole-grain mustard

Make-ahead and storage: Topping can be refrigerated overnight. Always keep plastic pressed directly against the surface of the topping when storing it, to avoid allowing a skin to form. Let topping sit at room temperature for 30 minutes to fully soften before using.
author: Leah Colins
